rule: The input is one induced 4-connected path of coloured cells on a plain plurality background. Unroll it cell by cell into an Nx1 column. Start at the path end (a cell with exactly one orthogonal path neighbour) that comes first in reading order. A colour may recur in non-adjacent runs.
scope: Construct an induced four-connected multicolour path and unroll it to a column, starting at the reading-order-first endpoint. Colour-run boundaries vary independently of geometric turns.

authored_scope: Supported: grid sides from 1..30 (default 10..22, a synthetic extension of the 16x16 fixtures); non-square grids; any background colour 0..9; paths of 2..30 cells (default 12..30) built from right-angle runs that go mostly down, but also left, right and occasionally up; 1..30 colour runs (default 2..6, each at least 2 cells); colours repeating in non-adjacent runs; explicit start/moves/runs reconstruction; output reversal when the generation start is not the reading-order-first end. Not supported: branching or self-touching paths, multiple paths, noise, outputs longer than 30 rows. By default, randomly grown paths whose end choice depends only on the reading-order tie-break are excluded; consistent_ends=False enables them.
authored_constraints: The path is induced: no two cells that are not consecutive along the path share an edge, so there are exactly two degree-1 ends.
Every path cell lies inside the grid; an explicit start is checked against the resolved width and height.
Neighbouring colour runs differ; no run colour equals the background.
The background count is strictly greater than every path colour's count. Random paths satisfy len(path) <= (w*h-1)//2.
Path length is 2..30, so the output has at most 30 rows.
By default, the reading-order-first end is also the reading-order-first path cell overall and is not right of the other end.
All retry loops are bounded; failure raises ValueError and never returns a fixed fallback scene.
